name: Islamic Studies — Life of Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)
subject: islamic-studies-life-of-prophet-muhammad-pbuh

questions.question_text: If a person is physically unable to perform the Hajj journey, what is the acceptable alternative prescribed by Islamic law?
options: Making a formal pledge (Nazar) to pray extra prayers
questions.explanation: Compensation (Fidya) through sacrifice or fasting is required for those who cannot physically complete the Hajj due to genuine inability.

questions.question_text: Which aspect of Iman (Faith) primarily involves believing in the unseen divine powers and miracles, such as Jinn, Angels, and the Day of Judgment?
questions.explanation: Belief in the Ghayb encompasses all matters beyond human sensory perception, including angels and the Day of Judgment.

questions.question_text: A student of Islamic Studies argues that Iman is not merely a cognitive agreement with Islamic tenets, but requires corresponding action and adherence. This perspective emphasizes Iman as:
questions.explanation: This interpretation views Iman as a comprehensive commitment that must manifest in the student's actions and behavior.

questions.question_text: Which pillar of Islam mandates the annual payment of a fixed sum of money on the shoulders of ability, calculated from accumulated wealth?
questions.explanation: Zakat is the obligatory charity paid on wealth that has reached a minimum threshold (Nisab) and has been held for a specific time.

questions.question_text: Which pillar of Iman (Faith) requires belief in the ultimate authority and divine wisdom behind creation and destiny?
questions.explanation: Qadar encompasses believing that everything that happens, good or bad, is by the pre-knowledge and will of Allah (SWT).

questions.question_text: Which pillar of Islam involves the ritual journey undertaken by all able-bodied Muslims to the holy city of Makkah, and is considered compulsory once financially and physically capable?
questions.explanation: Hajj is the pilgrimage to Makkah. Zakat is obligatory charity, Sawm is fasting, and Shahada is the declaration of faith.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is considered the foundational pillar (Arkan) of Iman, encompassing belief in the Book revealed to Prophet Muhammad (PBUH)?
options: Iman by the Day of Judgment (Iman bi al-Yawm al-Qiyamah)
Iman by the Books (Iman bi al-Kutub)
Iman by the Qadar (Iman bi al-Qadar)
Iman by the Angels (Iman bi al-Mala'ika)
questions.explanation: Belief in the Holy Books (Kutub) is a core pillar of Iman, specifically affirming the divine revelation, including the Qur'an.
